_README: Manual overrides. Anything set here WINS over every fetched source and is
published as-is with `"source": "manual-override"`.
BEFORE ADDING ONE: confirm the source is actually wrong. Open the raw feed and
read the record. An unfamiliar name is usually a real change, not a parse bug —
the pipeline exists because these answers change and memory goes stale. Every
senator record in senate.gov's XML carries a bioguide_id and a personal
senate.gov subdomain; a name with both is a sitting member, not a mis-parse.
An override that contradicts a correct source publishes a wrong answer to
people studying for their interview, which is the one outcome this whole
pipeline is built to prevent.
Legitimate uses: the morning after an inauguration, before the source updates;
a resignation or death the Clerk has not published yet; a source that has
genuinely broken and is serving stale or malformed data.
The build logs a warning whenever an override disagrees with its source, and a
notice once the source catches up so stale overrides are easy to find and
delete.
Shapes — each value may be a bare value or { value, reviewBy, reason }:
national.president|vicePresident|speaker|chiefJustice : "Full Name"
states.<CODE>.governor                                 : "Full Name"
states.<CODE>.senators                                 : ["Name", "Name"]
states.<CODE>.representatives.<district>               : "Full Name"
